audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tracks 'Twofold Hunt' in roughly twenty strings. No such ability exists — her Q is Twofold Hex. Worse, the thing the text describes ('Her escape', 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)') is not her Q at all, and the entry's own focus.letters reads ['W'].
audit.why: Two errors compounded: a garbled name, and that garbled name attached to the wrong slot's behaviour. Aurora's W is Across the Veil — a leap that lands her invisible with bonus Move Speed, 22/21/20/19/18. That is the escape the text means. A player following this entry looks for a blink on Q, finds a poke missile, and has no idea what he is supposed to be tracking. I renamed to Across the Veil so the name, the description and the existing ['W'] letter finally agree.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil (W), 22/21/20/19/18 — the leap, invisibility and escape. Twofold Hex (Q) is the 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 poke missile with a damaging recast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json — Q Twofold Hex; W Across the Veil 22/21/20/19/18

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings claim Aurora phases through mushrooms: 'use W spirit-walk to phase through mushroom walls' (wants.foe[2]), 'her W spirit-walk ... requires a landing zone free of shrooms' (mid), 'she can walk into the spirit realm mid-mushroom to avoid the slow, then blink back out' (late), 're-engage through late-game mushroom fields using her W phase' (whys[6]).
audit.why: This is a fabricated mechanic and it is the load-bearing assumption of the entire mid and late plan. Across the Veil grants invisibility and Move Speed on landing — nothing in it confers immunity to traps, terrain or ground effects. As written the entry tells a Teemo his one real win condition, the mushroom net, does not work on this opponent, which is precisely backwards: mushrooms are exactly how you punish a champion whose escape is a fixed-distance leap on a 22-second timer.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil is invisibility plus Move Speed. It grants no trap immunity — a mushroom on her landing spot still catches her.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json — W: 'leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible, and gaining Move Speed for a short duration of time' — no immunity clause

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings give Aurora a root — 'Root you with her Q follow-up' (wants.foe[1]) and 'With her Q root added to E blink, Aurora can now enter, root you in place, and exit' (whys[2]). early also refers to 'the moment she steps in and commits with her own root'.
audit.why: Twofold Hex does not root. The missile curses enemies it hits; the recast draws active curses back toward Aurora, damaging anyone caught along the way. There is no immobilising CC on her Q at all. Believing you will be rooted changes whether a Teemo commits to a trade or walks away from a winnable one, so the invented CC directly costs the player trades he should be taking.
audit.corrected: Twofold Hex: missile curses, recast drags the curse back for damage. No root. Her slows are on The Weirding (E) and Between Worlds (R).
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json — Q Twofold Hex description; E flags slow; R flags slow

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says Aurora will 'Blink in with E'.
audit.why: The Weirding sends out a blast then hops Aurora BACKWARD to safety — it is a disengage, not a gap-closer. Her engage leap is Across the Veil (W). The entry has her two mobility spells doing each other's jobs, so the 'she blinks in on you' fear is attached to the wrong cooldown and the wrong timer (E is 15/14/13/12/11, W is 22/21/20/19/18).
audit.corrected: The Weirding (E) hops her backward, 15s at rank 1 — disengage. Across the Veil (W) is the leap in, 22s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aurora.json — E: 'sending out a blast of spirit magic that damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward to safety', 15/14/13/12/11

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Teemo wins 59% over 461 games but the content win array gives Aurora four of seven stages (Aurora, Skill, Aurora, Aurora, Teemo, Skill, Aurora) and Teemo only one. Separately, the full layer's phases sides for the same matchup read Skill, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Teemo — a completely different picture.
audit.why: 59% is one of the strongest numbers in Teemo's whole table; a chart that hands the opponent the majority of stages, including the late game, is telling the player he is losing a lane he is in fact winning comfortably. I could only move one stage: the ±10% length rule makes 'Aurora' (6 chars) to 'Teemo' (5) an out-of-band edit that the applier will reject, so the four Aurora stages are physically unfixable through this mechanism. I changed win[5] (First item) from 'Skill' to 'Teemo' — same length, and it matches both the 59% headline and the full layer, which already sides Teemo at first item on the back of the Nashor's spike plus a live mushroom net.
audit.corrected: win[5] First item: Skill to Teemo. The remaining Aurora-sided stages need a human pass — see notes.

edits.before: Aurora owns the very opening of this lane because her Q poke reaches you at nearly the same range as your Toxic Shot, and her E blink means she can instantly exit any W-boosted chase before your poison DoT does meaningful work. Do not throw Blinding Shot speculatively at range — she has no reliance on basic attacks at levels 1-3, so your Q does not deny her damage output the way it punishes juggernauts. Instead, farm safely with E auto-poke, conserve Q for the moment she steps in and commits with her own root, and let her push the wave so you hold turret proximity for escapes. The lane is a mutual poke pattern at this stage; you are not losing it badly, but she sets the pace.
edits.after: Aurora owns the very opening of this lane because Twofold Hex reaches you at nearly the same range as your Toxic Shot, and The Weirding hops her clear of any W-boosted chase before your poison DoT does meaningful work. Do not throw Blinding Dart speculatively at range — she has almost no reliance on basic attacks, so your Q does not deny her damage output the way it punishes juggernauts. Instead, farm safely with E auto-poke, hold Q for the rare moment she steps up to auto, and let her push the wave so you keep turret proximity for escapes. Note she has no root: the Hex recast drags a curse back through you for damage, it does not lock you down.

edits.before: Your level 6 Noxious Trap placement is the genuine turning point of this matchup. Start sealing tribush, the river bush at the top of lane, and the pixel bush behind your turret — Aurora's W spirit-walk is what makes her dangerous in this window, but it requires a landing zone free of shrooms. Once those are covered, she has to walk into mushroom-slowed ground to re-enter the lane after any roam or retreat, which hands you free poison stacks and a positional advantage she cannot blink away from. Use W Move Quick to keep max E-poison range and never let her W into a clean spot behind you. She cannot all-in you if she has to walk through a poisoned corridor to reach you.
edits.after: Your level 6 Noxious Trap placement is the genuine turning point of this matchup. Start sealing tribush, the river bush at the top of lane, and the pixel bush behind your turret — Across the Veil is what makes her dangerous in this window: a 22-second leap that lands her invisible with bonus Move Speed. It grants no trap immunity, so a shroom sitting on her landing spot still catches her. Once those bushes are covered she has to cross mushroom-slowed ground to re-enter lane after any roam, which hands you free poison stacks. Use Move Quick to hold max poison range and never let her land cleanly behind you.

edits.before: Aurora's late-game AP burst and her W phase ability let her re-engage through mushroom fields that would stop other mages cold — she can walk into the spirit realm mid-mushroom to avoid the slow, then blink back out after the damage lands. Your Rylai's Scepter mitigates this partially, but a completed Zhonya's Hourglass lets her absorb your burst combo and answer back with a full rotation that your low HP pool cannot survive. The correct late-game answer is to avoid side-wave assignments where she can 1v1 you in open terrain; instead push your shroom-warded side, take plates, and rejoin the team where her blink re-engage has fewer safe angles and your team can follow up your slow-field setup.
edits.after: Aurora's late-game AP burst and Across the Veil let her re-engage through mushroom fields that would stop other mages cold — but the spirit realm is invisibility and Move Speed, not intangibility, so a shroom she lands on still slows and burns her. Your Rylai's covers the rest, though a completed Zhonya's Hourglass lets her absorb your burst and answer with a full rotation your HP pool cannot survive. Avoid side-wave assignments where she can 1v1 you in open terrain; push your shroom-warded side, take plates, and rejoin the team where her re-engage has fewer safe angles. Grievous Wounds matters: her passive heals off every spirit she pulls.

notes: LEVEL CHART, NEEDS YOUR DECISION: the packet is right that the content win array contradicts a 59% win rate, but I could only fix one stage. The ±10% length rule rejects 'Aurora' to 'Teemo' (6 chars to 5, ratio 0.83), so win[0], win[2], win[3] and win[6] cannot be flipped through a proposal at all — they need either a hand edit or an applier exemption for the win/side token fields, which are enums rather than prose and arguably should not be length-checked. I changed only win[5] (Skill to Teemo), which is length-safe and agrees with the full layer. The two layers also disagree wholesale here: content is Aurora/Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Teemo/Skill/Aurora while full is Skill/Teemo/Teemo/Skill/Skill/Teemo/Teemo. ITEM CONTRADICTION: the content layer builds its whole first-item plan around Rylai's Crystal Scepter while the full layer's Itemization says Nashor's Tooth then Liandry's Torment. I did not pick a winner — I cannot verify current Teemo build priority from the kit files and would not guess — but one of the two is wrong and a reader gets both. STILL CARRYING 'Twofold Hunt' after my edits: breakdown.early, breakdown.feeding, and report entries 1, 3, 9, 10, 12 and 13.
